heros.infro: Vladimir I of Kiev was the grand prince of Kiev who converted to Christianity in 988. He went on to baptize all of Kievan Russia. Churches today celebrate the feast day of Saint Vladimir.
heros.name: Vladimir I

heros.infro: Girart fought at the Battle of Fontenay as an ally of Lothair I while serving as Count of Paris.  Fifteen years later and upon Lothair's death, Girart ruled on behalf of his infant son whom had inherited large areas of land in Burgandy.  Much of his time spent as regent involved leading defensive campaigns againsts invading Northmen.
heros.name: Girart de Roussillon

heros.infro: A Jewish scholar and mystic, Joseph ben Ephraim Caro settled in Palestine around 1537 after years of travel and study following his family's expulsion from Spain in 1492. He wrote the last great codification of Jewish law in 1559. Caro published a condensed version called Prepared Table for everyday use in 1565, and it eventually became the written standard on Judaism.
heros.name: Joseph Caro

heros.infro: De Soto, a Spanish Conquistador, joined the conquest of Central America and Francisco Pizarro's assault on the Incas in Peru. Holy Roman Emperor Charles V made him Governor of Cuba, opening the door to conquering the North American mainland. De Soto landed in Florida in 1539 and explored the Carolinas,  Appalachians, Tennessee and Alabama. An expedition west probably made de Soto the first European to see the Mississippi River. He followed the Arkansas River to Oklahoma but returned to Florida without discovering gold or treasure.
heros.name: Hernando de Soto

heros.infro: Marcus Porcius Cato (234 B.C. –149 B.C.) was a Roman statesman, surnamed the Censor (Censorius), the Wise (Sapiens), the Ancient (Priscus), or the Elder (Maior), to distinguish him from Cato the Younger, his great-grandson.  He was born of an ancient Plebeian family who all were noted for military service but not for the discharge of the higher civil offices. He was bred, to agriculture, but, having attracted the notice of Lucius Valerius Flaccus, was brought to Rome, and successively held the offices of Cursus Honorum: Tribune, Quaestor, Aedile, Praetor, Consul, and finally Censor.
heros.name: Marcus Porcius Cato

heros.infro: In 1540, Anne became the fourth wife of England's King Henry VIII after being chosen for the job by Thomas Cromwell to seal an alliance with German Protestants. Evidently, Henry thought her not the most attractive of German princesses, and he had their unconsummated marriage annulled after 6 months. Keeping her head may have been her greatest achievement.
heros.name: Anne of Cleves

heros.infro: A ferocious Viking warrior, Rorik has spent over thirty years at war.  Most of his campaigns took place in Friesland where he ruled over several different areas off and on including Dorestad and Utrecht.
heros.name: Rorik of Dorestad

heros.infro: Roman statesman and general, He was responsible for most of Octavian
heros.name: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa

heros.infro: The only son of Henry the Proud, Henry the Lion controlled a vast swath of land in Northeastern Europe.  He gained and held these these lands through military skill, shrewd political maneuvering and the legacy of his four grandparents.  Ruling over large portions of Bavaria and Saxony from 1142 until 1180 his reign was long and prosperous and during its tenure he founded the historic cities of Munich and Lubeck.  His empire was eventually picked apart in 1181 by a large coalition of jealous Germanic princes led by his cousin Frederick I Barbarossa.  Humbled but still proud Henry lived out his days sponsoring art and architecture as the Duke of Brunswick until his death in 1195.
heros.name: Henry the Lion

heros.infro: England's King Henry VIII was married to Catherine of Aragon when, in 1527, he began a love affair with Anne Boleyn, daughter of a Protestant, Pro-Reformation family that had risen to prominence at court. After an ugly, protracted battle against Catherine, the Catholic Church, and the Pope, Henry's marriage to Catherine was annulled. He married Anne who was crowned Queen and gave birth to a daughter in 1533. Like Catherine, Anne failed to bear a son, and she was beheaded on trumped-up adultery charges in 1536. The last word was Anne's--her daughter was crowned Elizabeth I in 1558.
heros.name: Anne Boleyn

heros.infro: Joan's lineage and beauty guaranteed her marriage into powerful English ruling families at an early age.  Although she has very little experience in an overt leadership position, she holds the ear of England's most powerful monarchs.
heros.name: Joan of Kent

heros.infro: William III was a Prince of Orange, who governed the Dutch Republic. Later he reigned with his wife MaryII over England, Scotland and Ireland. He fought in several wars against Louis XIV.
heros.name: William III

heros.infro: The daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, Elizabeth I served both as the Queen of England and the Queen of Ireland.  Although most consider her weak in military matters, Elizabeth rigorously supported art and literature which led to a golden age in English history.
heros.name: Elizabeth I

heros.infro: French theologian John Calvin was educated in Paris and Orléans. He converted to Reformed Protestantism and wrote the definitive work on its theology, which minimizes free will. He also wrote a model for church government later adopted by the Presbyterians. For 30 years, Calvin tried to establish Geneva, Switzerland, as a haven for followers of his version of church doctrine and moral living. The Puritans in England and North America and followers in Scotland, the Netherlands, and France were strongly influenced by Calvinist doctrine.
heros.name: John Calvin

heros.infro: The last King of the House of York, Richard III seized power after the death of his brother, Edward IV.  He had Edward's two sons, Edward V and Richard, placed in the Tower of London to keep them safe, and they were never seen again.  His reign lasted only two years, ending with his death at the Battle of Bosworth field, making him the second and last English king to die in battle.  Richard is more favorably remembered in the northern parts of England.  Previous to his ascension, he had done much to improve the living conditions of the commoners as Governor of the North.
heros.name: Richard III of England

heros.infro: A financier and diplomat, Sir Thomas Gresham founded the Royal Exchange. He influenced the economic policy of the court of Elizabeth I of England through his work with William Cecil, founded Gresham College in 1579, and started the series of public lectures that evolved into the Royal Society.
heros.name: Sir Thomas Gresham

heros.infro: Manius Curius Dentatus (d. 270 B.C.) was a Roman general, conqueror of the Samnites and Pyrrhus, and king of Epirus.  He is said to have been called Dentatus because he was born with his teeth already grown. Dentatus was tribune of the plebs sometime between 298 and 291 B.C..  As consul in 290 B.C., in conjunction with his colleague P. Cornelius Rufinus, he gained a decisive victory over the Samnites, which put an end to the war that had lasted fifty years.
heros.name: Manius Curius Dentatus

heros.infro: Utu-hengal was one of the first native kings of Sumer after centuries of Akkadian and Gutian rule.  As governor of Uruk, with the aid of other cities, he revolted against Gutian rule in the 22nd century B.C. and established himself as the king of Sumer.  He was unable to maintain power and reigned for only 7 years
heros.name: Utu-hengal

heros.infro: A  religious nonconformist, Browne's followers were the first sect to separate from the Anglican Church following the Reformation. The Brownists wanted immediate changes to the Anglican doctrine and urged others to leave the church in protest. Browne reconciled himself to the Anglican Church in 1591, but his ideals of church government were championed later by the Congregationalists.
heros.name: Robert Browne

heros.infro: A member of the prominent Guise branch of the French Royal family, Claude was created Duke of Guise in 1528 after many French military victories. Claude's brother Charles became Cardinal of Guise in 1550 and his sister Mary married James V of Scotland and gave birth to Mary, Queen of Scots.
heros.name: Claude de Lorraine. Duke of Guise
